description: A 2024 systematic review identified denial and dismissal of symptoms, delayed diagnosis, negative experiences with staff, gender bias, the need for self-advocacy, stigmatisation of mental health by clinicians, and anxiety and trauma - concluding women's experiences are overwhelmingly negative.
energy_note: Seven themes, and the seventh is the trauma of the first six.

aspect: The delays are measurable and specific
description: Longer diagnostic intervals for multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis, acute coronary syndromes, lupus and chronic pain, with cognitive heuristics disproportionately categorising women's symptoms as functional or anxiety-related.

aspect: And the treatment gap is measurable too
description: Women attending emergency departments with severe stomach pain waited almost 33% longer than men with the same presentation.
energy_note: A third longer, for the same pain.

description: He has her file open and does not look at it. 'You're quite anxious, aren't you.' She says she is in pain. 'Pain does make people anxious.' He offers an SSRI and a leaflet on sleep hygiene. It is endometriosis, diagnosed four years later.
energy_note: Four years, and the first note said anxious.

aspect: Being dismissed makes people stop attending
description: Patients whose conditions are dismissed may stop seeking care entirely, which produces later presentation, worse outcomes, and a record that appears to show non-compliance.
energy_note: She stops going, and that goes in the notes too.
